1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE

Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease characterised by intense pruritus and eczematous lesions. In Singapore, the prevalence of AD in adults is estimated at approximately 11%, with moderate-to-severe disease representing a significant burden on quality of life and healthcare resources. Current treatment paradigms include topical corticosteroids (TCS), topical calcineurin inhibitors (TCI), phototherapy, and systemic immunosuppressants. However, many patients experience inadequate response, loss of effect, or intolerable adverse effects, highlighting an unmet medical need for novel, targeted therapies.

PT-101 is an investigational humanised monoclonal antibody designed to selectively bind to the IL-13 receptor alpha-1 subunit, thereby inhibiting IL-13-mediated signalling. IL-13 is a key cytokine in the pathogenesis of AD, driving epidermal barrier dysfunction, inflammation, and pruritus. By blocking this pathway, PT-101 is hypothesised to improve skin clearance and reduce symptom burden in patients with moderate-to-severe AD. Preclinical studies and early-phase clinical trials have demonstrated a favourable safety profile and promising efficacy signals, supporting further investigation in a Phase 2 setting.

2. STUDY OBJECTIVES

2.1 Primary Objective
To evaluate the efficacy of PT-101 compared with placebo in reducing the signs and symptoms of AD, as measured by the proportion of participants achieving an Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score of 0 or 1 with at least a 2-point improvement from baseline at Week 16.

2.2 Secondary Objectives
• To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on pruritus, as measured by the change from baseline in the Peak Pruritus Numeric Rating Scale (PP-NRS) weekly average.
• To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on the extent and severity of AD, as measured by the change from baseline in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score.
• To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on health-related quality of life, as measured by the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI).
• To assess the safety and tolerability of PT-101, including the incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs).

3. STUDY DESIGN

This is a Phase 2, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Approximately 240 participants will be randomised in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive one of two dose levels of PT-101 (low dose, high dose) or matching placebo.
Secondary endpoints include:

- Change from baseline in the Peak Pruritus Numeric Rating Scale (PP-NRS) weekly average at Week 16.
- Change from baseline in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score at Week 16.
- Change from baseline in the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) total score at Week 16.
- Proportion of participants achieving EASI-75 (≥75% improvement from baseline) at Week 16.
- Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), and adverse events of special interest (AESIs).

4.3 Exploratory Endpoints

Exploratory endpoints include:

- Change from baseline in serum levels of total IgE and IL-13-related biomarkers.
- Pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters of PT-101, including maximum observed concentration (Cmax), time to maximum concentration (Tmax), and area under the concentration-time curve (AUC).
- Incidence of anti-drug antibodies (ADA) and neutralising antibodies (NAb) against PT-101.
- Change from baseline in sleep disturbance scores as assessed by the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Sleep-Related Impairment Short Form.

5. STATISTICAL METHODS

5.1 Sample Size Determination

Approximately 240 participants will be randomised in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive low-dose PT-101, high-dose PT-101, or matching placebo. The sample size calculation assumes a placebo response rate of 15% for the primary endpoint, and treatment response rates of 35% and 45% for low- and high-dose PT-101, respectively. With 80 participants per arm, the study will have approximately 85% power to detect a difference of 20 percentage points between the high-dose arm and placebo at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05, using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by baseline IGA score (2 vs 3) and prior systemic therapy use (yes vs no). No adjustment for multiplicity is planned for the secondary endpoints; results will be interpreted with appropriate caution.

The protocol_approval_date for TID-2210 is 2024-05-14. Record status: current.

5.2 Analysis Populations

- Full Analysis Set (FAS): All randomised participants who receive at least one dose of study intervention. Participants will be analysed according to the treatment arm to which they were randomised, regardless of actual treatment received.
- Per-Protocol Set (PPS): A subset of the FAS, comprising participants who complete the study without major protocol deviations that could significantly affect the efficacy evaluation.
- Safety Analysis Set: All participants who receive at least one dose of study intervention, analysed according to the actual treatment received.

5.3 Primary Efficacy Analysis

The primary endpoint will be analysed using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test, stratified by baseline IGA score and prior systemic therapy use. Missing data for the primary endpoint will be handled using multiple imputation under a missing-at-random assumption, with sensitivity analyses using non-responder imputation and tipping-point analysis.

5.4 Secondary and Exploratory Analyses

Continuous secondary endpoints will be analysed using a mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM) with treatment arm, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline IGA score, and prior systemic therapy use as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Categorical secondary endpoints will be analysed using logistic regression with the same covariates. Exploratory endpoints will be summarised descriptively; PK parameters will be derived using non-compartmental methods and summarised by dose level and visit.

5.5 Safety Analyses

Safety data will be summarised descriptively by treatment arm. TEAEs will be coded using MedDRA (Version 26.1) and summarised by system organ class and preferred term. Laboratory parameters, vital signs, and ECGs will be summarised using change-from-baseline descriptive statistics. AESIs, including injection-site reactions and hypersensitivity events, will be listed individually and reviewed on an ongoing basis by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB).

6. STUDY INTERVENTION AND CONCOMITANT MEDICATIONS

6.1 Description of Study Intervention

PT-101 is supplied as a sterile, preservative-free solution for intravenous infusion, presented in single-use vials containing 500 mg of active substance per vial. Each vial is intended for single use only; any unused portion must be discarded in accordance with institutional biohazard waste procedures. The investigational product should be stored at 2°C to 8°C, protected from light, and must not be frozen or shaken.

6.2 Dosing Regimen

The dosing_regimen for PT-101 is 500 mg/m2 every 3 weeks. Record status: current. The dose is calculated based on the participant's body surface area (BSA) determined at the Screening Visit and will be recalculated at the start of each treatment cycle if the participant's weight has changed by more than 10% from the most recent recorded weight. BSA will be calculated using the Mosteller formula:

BSA (m²) = √[(height (cm) × weight (kg)) / 3600]

The calculated dose will be rounded to the nearest 10 mg for preparation. Each cycle is defined as a 21-day period. Study intervention will be administered on Day 1 of each cycle, following completion of all pre-dose assessments and confirmation that the participant continues to meet the criteria for dosing as specified in Section 6.4.

6.3 Administration Procedures

PT-101 will be administered as an intravenous infusion over 90 minutes (± 15 minutes) using an infusion pump. The infusion rate may be reduced or interrupted in the event of infusion-related reactions, per Section 6.5.2. Pre-medication with an antihistamine (e.g., diphenhydramine 25–50 mg oral or IV) and an antipyretic (e.g., paracetamol 500–1000 mg oral) is recommended 30–60 minutes prior to the start of each infusion for the first two cycles; prophylaxis may be continued at the discretion of the Investigator for subsequent cycles.

The infusion line must be primed with 0.9% sodium chloride for injection. PT-101 must not be co-administered through the same intravenous line with any other medicinal product. After the infusion is complete, the line will be flushed with 0.9% sodium chloride for injection. Participants will be observed for at least 60 minutes after the end of the infusion for signs of hypersensitivity or infusion-related reactions. The observation period may be extended at the discretion of the Investigator.

6.4 Criteria for Dosing on Day 1 of Each Cycle

Dosing on Day 1 of each cycle may proceed only if the following criteria are met based on laboratory assessments obtained within 72 hours prior to dosing:

- Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1.5 × 10⁹/L
- Platelet count ≥ 100 × 10⁹/L
- Haemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL
- Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤ 3.0 × upper limit of normal (ULN), unless due to documented liver metastasis, in which case ≤ 5.0 × ULN
- Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × ULN (participants with documented Gilbert's syndrome may be enrolled with total bilirubin ≤ 3.0 × ULN)
- Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m², calculated using the CKD-EPI equation
- No unresolved Grade ≥ 2 toxicity (per CTCAE Version 5.0) considered related to PT-101, with the exception of alopecia, fatigue Grade 2, or laboratory abnormalities that are not clinically significant per the Investigator's judgement

If the participant does not meet the above criteria, dosing will be delayed. Re-assessment will be performed at least weekly until the criteria are met. Dosing delays of more than 3 weeks from the scheduled date will require discussion with the Medical Monitor before resuming treatment.

6.5 Dose Modifications

6.5.1 Haematological Toxicity

For Grade 3 or Grade 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia considered related to PT-101:

- First occurrence: Interrupt dosing until resolution to Grade ≤ 1 or baseline. Upon recovery, resume at the same dose level (500 mg/m²).
- Second occurrence: Upon recovery, reduce the dose to 400 mg/m².
- Third occurrence: Upon recovery, reduce the dose to 300 mg/m².
- Fourth occurrence or failure to recover within 14 days: Discontinue PT-101 permanently.

**1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE**

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) commonly co-exist and share underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, including insulin resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, and dysregulated lipid metabolism. Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), the progressive form of NAFLD, is a leading cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality. There remains an unmet medical need for therapies that improve both glycaemic control and hepatic steatosis in this patient population.

PT-101 is an investigational, once-daily, oral small molecule being developed for the treatment of T2DM with concomitant hepatic steatosis. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that PT-101 improves insulin sensitivity and reduces hepatic triglyceride content in animal models of diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance. This first-in-patient study will evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of PT-101 in the target population.

**2. STUDY OBJECTIVES AND ENDPOINTS**

**2.1 Primary Objective**

To evaluate the effect of PT-101, compared with placebo, on hepatic steatosis, as measured by magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF), after 24 weeks of treatment.

**2.2 Secondary Objectives**

- To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on glycaemic control, as measured by change in HbA1c.
- To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on body weight.
- To evaluate the safety and tolerability of PT-101.

Novena Health Research Centre's inclusion_criteria_version is IC-2024-05. Record status: current.

**2.3 Primary Endpoint**

Change from baseline to Week 24 in hepatic steatosis, as measured by MRI-PDFF (absolute percentage point change).

**2.4 Secondary Endpoints**

- Change from baseline to Week 24 in HbA1c.
- Change from baseline to Week 24 in body weight.
- Proportion of participants achieving ≥30% relative reduction in MRI-PDFF from baseline to Week 24.
- Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs).

**3. STUDY DESIGN**

This is a Phase 2, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study. Approximately 120 participants will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio to receive PT-101 25 mg once daily or matching placebo for 24 weeks.

The study will consist of a screening period (up to 6 weeks), a 24-week double-blind treatment period, and a follow-up visit at Week 28 (4 weeks after the last dose). Randomisation will be stratified by baseline HbA1c (<8.5% vs ≥8.5%) and baseline MRI-PDFF (<15% vs ≥15%).

Participants who complete the 24-week treatment period and the Week 28 follow-up visit will be considered to have completed the study. Participants who discontinue study drug early will be asked to complete an early termination visit and a follow-up visit 28 days after the last dose.

**4. STUDY POPULATION**

The study population will consist of adult male and female participants, aged 30 to 70 years, with a diagnosis of T2DM and confirmed hepatic steatosis. Participants must be receiving a stable dose of metformin monotherapy (≥1500 mg/day or maximum tolerated dose) for at least 8 weeks prior to screening, or be treatment-naïve with an HbA1c of 7.0% to 10.5% at screening.

Participants must be willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. Written informed consent must be obtained prior to any study-related procedure.

**5. INCLUSION CRITERIA**
**5.1 Inclusion Criteria**

Participants must meet all of the following criteria to be enrolled in the study:

1. Male or female, aged 30 to 70 years, inclusive, at the time of informed consent.
2. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) for at least 6 months prior to screening.
3. HbA1c between 7.0% and 10.5%, inclusive, at screening (central laboratory).
4. Confirmed hepatic steatosis, defined as MRI-PDFF ≥ 10% at screening (central reading).
5. Receiving a stable dose of metformin monotherapy (≥1500 mg/day or maximum tolerated dose) for at least 8 weeks prior to screening, OR treatment-naïve with HbA1c of 7.0% to 10.5% at screening.
6. Body mass index (BMI) between 25.0 and 40.0 kg/m², inclusive, at screening.
7. Willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.
8. Written informed consent obtained prior to any study-related procedure.

**5.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Participants who meet any of the following criteria will be excluded from the study:

1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus, or a history of diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state within 6 months prior to screening.
2. Use of any glucose-lowering medication other than metformin within 12 weeks prior to screening, or anticipated need for such medication during the study.
3. History of bariatric surgery or other gastrointestinal surgery that could affect absorption of study drug.
4. Known cirrhosis, or evidence of clinically significant liver disease other than non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), including but not limited to chronic hepatitis B or C, autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, or Wilson's disease.
5. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) > 3 × upper limit of normal (ULN) at screening.
6. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 60 mL/min/1.73 m² at screening (CKD-EPI equation).
7. Uncontrolled hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure > 160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure > 100 mmHg at screening, despite antihypertensive therapy.
8. History of pancreatitis, or fasting serum triglycerides > 5.6 mmol/L at screening.
9. Active malignancy, or history of malignancy within 5 years prior to screening, except for adequately treated basal cell carcinoma or carcinoma in situ of the cervix.
10. Known hypersensitivity to PT-101 or any of its excipients.
11. Participation in any other interventional clinical trial within 30 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to screening.
12. Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test at screening and must agree to use a highly effective method of contraception throughout the study and for 30 days after the last dose.
13. Any other condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would make the participant unsuitable for the study or could interfere with the participant's ability to complete the study.

**6. SAFETY MONITORING**

**6.1 Safety Variables**

Safety will be assessed throughout the study by monitoring the following:

- Adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs).
- Clinical laboratory tests (haematology, biochemistry, liver function, renal function, urinalysis).
- Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, body temperature).
- 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG).
- Physical examination findings.
- Concomitant medication use.

**6.2 Safety Monitoring Plan**

An independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will be convened to review accumulating safety data. The DSMB will include members with expertise in hepatology, endocrinology, and clinical pharmacology. The DSMB will meet at the following time points:

- After the first 20 participants have completed 12 weeks of treatment.
- After all participants have completed 24 weeks of treatment.
- At any time if a safety concern is identified by the sponsor or the investigator.

The DSMB will provide written recommendations to the sponsor regarding the continuation, modification, or termination of the study. The sponsor will communicate these recommendations to the relevant ethics committees and health authorities as required.
**7. ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS**

**7.1 Independent Ethics Committee / Institutional Review Board**

The protocol, the informed consent form, and all participant-facing materials will be submitted to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of each participating site for review and written approval prior to study initiation. The study will not commence at any site until written IRB approval has been obtained. Any amendments to the protocol or informed consent form will be submitted for IRB review and approval before implementation, except where necessary to eliminate an immediate hazard to participants.

The study will be conducted in accordance with the ethical principles that have their origin in the Declaration of Helsinki, the SGGCP, and the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) regulations. Written informed consent will be obtained from each participant before any study-specific procedure is performed. documents.content:
A Phase 2, Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of PT-101 in Participants with Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis

Protocol Version 3.1
Effective Date: 14 May 2024

Supersedes: Version 3.0 (dated 02 January 2024)

Sponsor: Meridian Biopharma Pte. Ltd.
8 Science Park Drive, #04-01
Singapore 118231

Coordinating Investigator: A/Prof. Lim Wei Ming, Singapore General Hospital

Confidentiality Statement
This document contains confidential information proprietary to Meridian Biopharma Pte. Ltd. Any unauthorised use, copying, or disclosure is prohibited without prior written consent. This protocol is intended solely for use by the Investigator, sub-investigators, study coordinators, and relevant Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Health Sciences Authority (HSA) personnel.

---

REVISION HISTORY

| Version | Date | Description of Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 12 Mar 2022 | Original protocol |
| 2.0 | 05 Sep 2022 | Amendment: Updated inclusion criteria for prior therapy; clarified washout period; added Singapore site |
| 3.0 | 02 Jan 2024 | Amendment: Revised primary endpoint definition; updated safety monitoring plan |
| 3.1 | 14 May 2024 | Amendment: Clarified eligibility criteria for prior biologic use; added Note on TCS/TACI use; updated statistical analysis section |

The current protocol_version for TID-2210 is Version 3.1. Record status: current. This version is effective from 14 May 2024 and supersedes all previous versions. Sites must use Version 3.1 for all screening and enrolment activities commencing on or after this date.

---

1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE

Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease characterised by intense pruritus and eczematous lesions. In Singapore, the prevalence of AD in adults is estimated at approximately 11%, with moderate-to-severe disease representing a significant burden on quality of life and healthcare resources. Current treatment paradigms include topical corticosteroids (TCS), topical calcineurin inhibitors (TCI), phototherapy, and systemic immunosuppressants. However, many patients experience inadequate response, loss of effect, or intolerable adverse effects, highlighting an unmet medical need for novel, targeted therapies.

PT-101 is an investigational humanised monoclonal antibody designed to selectively bind to the IL-13 receptor alpha-1 subunit, thereby inhibiting IL-13-mediated signalling. IL-13 is a key cytokine in the pathogenesis of AD, driving epidermal barrier dysfunction, inflammation, and pruritus. By blocking this pathway, PT-101 is hypothesised to improve skin clearance and reduce symptom burden in patients with moderate-to-severe AD. Preclinical studies and early-phase clinical trials have demonstrated a favourable safety profile and promising efficacy signals, supporting further investigation in a Phase 2 setting.

2. STUDY OBJECTIVES

2.1 Primary Objective
To evaluate the efficacy of PT-101 compared with placebo in reducing the signs and symptoms of AD, as measured by the proportion of participants achieving an Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score of 0 or 1 with at least a 2-point improvement from baseline at Week 16.

2.2 Secondary Objectives
• To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on pruritus, as measured by the change from baseline in the Peak Pruritus Numeric Rating Scale (PP-NRS) weekly average.
• To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on the extent and severity of AD, as measured by the change from baseline in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score.
• To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on health-related quality of life, as measured by the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI).
• To assess the safety and tolerability of PT-101, including the incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs).

3. STUDY DESIGN

This is a Phase 2, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Approximately 240 participants will be randomised in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive one of two dose levels of PT-101 (low dose, high dose) or matching placebo.

documents.content:
Secondary endpoints include:

- Change from baseline in the Peak Pruritus Numeric Rating Scale (PP-NRS) weekly average at Week 16.
- Change from baseline in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score at Week 16.
- Change from baseline in the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) total score at Week 16.
- Proportion of participants achieving EASI-75 (≥75% improvement from baseline) at Week 16.
- Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), and adverse events of special interest (AESIs).

4.3 Exploratory Endpoints

Exploratory endpoints include:

- Change from baseline in serum levels of total IgE and IL-13-related biomarkers.
- Pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters of PT-101, including maximum observed concentration (Cmax), time to maximum concentration (Tmax), and area under the concentration-time curve (AUC).
- Incidence of anti-drug antibodies (ADA) and neutralising antibodies (NAb) against PT-101.
- Change from baseline in sleep disturbance scores as assessed by the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Sleep-Related Impairment Short Form.

5. STATISTICAL METHODS

5.1 Sample Size Determination

Approximately 240 participants will be randomised in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive low-dose PT-101, high-dose PT-101, or matching placebo. The sample size calculation assumes a placebo response rate of 15% for the primary endpoint, and treatment response rates of 35% and 45% for low- and high-dose PT-101, respectively. With 80 participants per arm, the study will have approximately 85% power to detect a difference of 20 percentage points between the high-dose arm and placebo at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05, using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by baseline IGA score (2 vs 3) and prior systemic therapy use (yes vs no). No adjustment for multiplicity is planned for the secondary endpoints; results will be interpreted with appropriate caution.

The protocol_approval_date for TID-2210 is 2024-05-14. Record status: current.

5.2 Analysis Populations

- Full Analysis Set (FAS): All randomised participants who receive at least one dose of study intervention. Participants will be analysed according to the treatment arm to which they were randomised, regardless of actual treatment received.
- Per-Protocol Set (PPS): A subset of the FAS, comprising participants who complete the study without major protocol deviations that could significantly affect the efficacy evaluation.
- Safety Analysis Set: All participants who receive at least one dose of study intervention, analysed according to the actual treatment received.

5.3 Primary Efficacy Analysis

The primary endpoint will be analysed using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test, stratified by baseline IGA score and prior systemic therapy use. Missing data for the primary endpoint will be handled using multiple imputation under a missing-at-random assumption, with sensitivity analyses using non-responder imputation and tipping-point analysis.

5.4 Secondary and Exploratory Analyses

Continuous secondary endpoints will be analysed using a mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM) with treatment arm, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline IGA score, and prior systemic therapy use as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Categorical secondary endpoints will be analysed using logistic regression with the same covariates. Exploratory endpoints will be summarised descriptively; PK parameters will be derived using non-compartmental methods and summarised by dose level and visit.

5.5 Safety Analyses

Safety data will be summarised descriptively by treatment arm. TEAEs will be coded using MedDRA (Version 26.1) and summarised by system organ class and preferred term. Laboratory parameters, vital signs, and ECGs will be summarised using change-from-baseline descriptive statistics. AESIs, including injection-site reactions and hypersensitivity events, will be listed individually and reviewed on an ongoing basis by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB).

Clinical Study Protocol TID-2210
Investigational Product: PT-101
Protocol Version 3.0 (Effective 14-May-2024)
Amendment History: Amendment 2 (14-May-2024); Amendment 1 (02-Jan-2024); Original (01-Sep-2023)

---

6. STUDY INTERVENTION AND CONCOMITANT MEDICATIONS

6.1 Description of Study Intervention

PT-101 is supplied as a sterile, preservative-free solution for intravenous infusion, presented in single-use vials containing 500 mg of active substance per vial. Each vial is intended for single use only; any unused portion must be discarded in accordance with institutional biohazard waste procedures. The investigational product should be stored at 2°C to 8°C, protected from light, and must not be frozen or shaken.

6.2 Dosing Regimen

The dosing_regimen for PT-101 is 500 mg/m2 every 3 weeks. Record status: current. The dose is calculated based on the participant's body surface area (BSA) determined at the Screening Visit and will be recalculated at the start of each treatment cycle if the participant's weight has changed by more than 10% from the most recent recorded weight. BSA will be calculated using the Mosteller formula:

BSA (m²) = √[(height (cm) × weight (kg)) / 3600]

The calculated dose will be rounded to the nearest 10 mg for preparation. Each cycle is defined as a 21-day period. Study intervention will be administered on Day 1 of each cycle, following completion of all pre-dose assessments and confirmation that the participant continues to meet the criteria for dosing as specified in Section 6.4.

6.3 Administration Procedures

PT-101 will be administered as an intravenous infusion over 90 minutes (± 15 minutes) using an infusion pump. The infusion rate may be reduced or interrupted in the event of infusion-related reactions, per Section 6.5.2. Pre-medication with an antihistamine (e.g., diphenhydramine 25–50 mg oral or IV) and an antipyretic (e.g., paracetamol 500–1000 mg oral) is recommended 30–60 minutes prior to the start of each infusion for the first two cycles; prophylaxis may be continued at the discretion of the Investigator for subsequent cycles.

The infusion line must be primed with 0.9% sodium chloride for injection. PT-101 must not be co-administered through the same intravenous line with any other medicinal product. After the infusion is complete, the line will be flushed with 0.9% sodium chloride for injection. Participants will be observed for at least 60 minutes after the end of the infusion for signs of hypersensitivity or infusion-related reactions. The observation period may be extended at the discretion of the Investigator.

6.4 Criteria for Dosing on Day 1 of Each Cycle

Dosing on Day 1 of each cycle may proceed only if the following criteria are met based on laboratory assessments obtained within 72 hours prior to dosing:

- Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1.5 × 10⁹/L
- Platelet count ≥ 100 × 10⁹/L
- Haemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL
- Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤ 3.0 × upper limit of normal (ULN), unless due to documented liver metastasis, in which case ≤ 5.0 × ULN
- Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × ULN (participants with documented Gilbert's syndrome may be enrolled with total bilirubin ≤ 3.0 × ULN)
- Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m², calculated using the CKD-EPI equation
- No unresolved Grade ≥ 2 toxicity (per CTCAE Version 5.0) considered related to PT-101, with the exception of alopecia, fatigue Grade 2, or laboratory abnormalities that are not clinically significant per the Investigator's judgement

If the participant does not meet the above criteria, dosing will be delayed. Re-assessment will be performed at least weekly until the criteria are met. Dosing delays of more than 3 weeks from the scheduled date will require discussion with the Medical Monitor before resuming treatment.

6.5 Dose Modifications

6.5.1 Haematological Toxicity

For Grade 3 or Grade 4 neutropenia or thrombocytopenia considered related to PT-101:

- First occurrence: Interrupt dosing until resolution to Grade ≤ 1 or baseline. Upon recovery, resume at the same dose level (500 mg/m²).
- Second occurrence: Upon recovery, reduce the dose to 400 mg/m².
- Third occurrence: Upon recovery, reduce the dose to 300 mg/m².
- Fourth occurrence or failure to recover within 14 days: Discontinue PT-101 permanently.

**1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE**

Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) commonly co-exist and share underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, including insulin resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, and dysregulated lipid metabolism. Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), the progressive form of NAFLD, is a leading cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality. There remains an unmet medical need for therapies that improve both glycaemic control and hepatic steatosis in this patient population.

PT-101 is an investigational, once-daily, oral small molecule being developed for the treatment of T2DM with concomitant hepatic steatosis. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that PT-101 improves insulin sensitivity and reduces hepatic triglyceride content in animal models of diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance. This first-in-patient study will evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of PT-101 in the target population.

**2. STUDY OBJECTIVES AND ENDPOINTS**

**2.1 Primary Objective**

To evaluate the effect of PT-101, compared with placebo, on hepatic steatosis, as measured by magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF), after 24 weeks of treatment.

**2.2 Secondary Objectives**

- To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on glycaemic control, as measured by change in HbA1c.
- To evaluate the effect of PT-101 on body weight.
- To evaluate the safety and tolerability of PT-101.

Novena Health Research Centre's inclusion_criteria_version is IC-2024-05. Record status: current.

**2.3 Primary Endpoint**

Change from baseline to Week 24 in hepatic steatosis, as measured by MRI-PDFF (absolute percentage point change).

**2.4 Secondary Endpoints**

- Change from baseline to Week 24 in HbA1c.
- Change from baseline to Week 24 in body weight.
- Proportion of participants achieving ≥30% relative reduction in MRI-PDFF from baseline to Week 24.
- Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs).

**3. STUDY DESIGN**

This is a Phase 2, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study. Approximately 120 participants will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio to receive PT-101 25 mg once daily or matching placebo for 24 weeks.

The study will consist of a screening period (up to 6 weeks), a 24-week double-blind treatment period, and a follow-up visit at Week 28 (4 weeks after the last dose). Randomisation will be stratified by baseline HbA1c (<8.5% vs ≥8.5%) and baseline MRI-PDFF (<15% vs ≥15%).

Participants who complete the 24-week treatment period and the Week 28 follow-up visit will be considered to have completed the study. Participants who discontinue study drug early will be asked to complete an early termination visit and a follow-up visit 28 days after the last dose.

**4. STUDY POPULATION**

The study population will consist of adult male and female participants, aged 30 to 70 years, with a diagnosis of T2DM and confirmed hepatic steatosis. Participants must be receiving a stable dose of metformin monotherapy (≥1500 mg/day or maximum tolerated dose) for at least 8 weeks prior to screening, or be treatment-naïve with an HbA1c of 7.0% to 10.5% at screening.

Participants must be willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. Written informed consent must be obtained prior to any study-related procedure.

**5. INCLUSION CRITERIA**

documents.content:
**5.1 Inclusion Criteria**

Participants must meet all of the following criteria to be enrolled in the study:

1. Male or female, aged 30 to 70 years, inclusive, at the time of informed consent.
2. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) for at least 6 months prior to screening.
3. HbA1c between 7.0% and 10.5%, inclusive, at screening (central laboratory).
4. Confirmed hepatic steatosis, defined as MRI-PDFF ≥ 10% at screening (central reading).
5. Receiving a stable dose of metformin monotherapy (≥1500 mg/day or maximum tolerated dose) for at least 8 weeks prior to screening, OR treatment-naïve with HbA1c of 7.0% to 10.5% at screening.
6. Body mass index (BMI) between 25.0 and 40.0 kg/m², inclusive, at screening.
7. Willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.
8. Written informed consent obtained prior to any study-related procedure.

**5.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Participants who meet any of the following criteria will be excluded from the study:

1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus, or a history of diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state within 6 months prior to screening.
2. Use of any glucose-lowering medication other than metformin within 12 weeks prior to screening, or anticipated need for such medication during the study.
3. History of bariatric surgery or other gastrointestinal surgery that could affect absorption of study drug.
4. Known cirrhosis, or evidence of clinically significant liver disease other than non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), including but not limited to chronic hepatitis B or C, autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, or Wilson's disease.
5. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) > 3 × upper limit of normal (ULN) at screening.
6. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 60 mL/min/1.73 m² at screening (CKD-EPI equation).
7. Uncontrolled hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure > 160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure > 100 mmHg at screening, despite antihypertensive therapy.
8. History of pancreatitis, or fasting serum triglycerides > 5.6 mmol/L at screening.
9. Active malignancy, or history of malignancy within 5 years prior to screening, except for adequately treated basal cell carcinoma or carcinoma in situ of the cervix.
10. Known hypersensitivity to PT-101 or any of its excipients.
11. Participation in any other interventional clinical trial within 30 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to screening.
12. Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test at screening and must agree to use a highly effective method of contraception throughout the study and for 30 days after the last dose.
13. Any other condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would make the participant unsuitable for the study or could interfere with the participant's ability to complete the study.

**6. SAFETY MONITORING**

**6.1 Safety Variables**

Safety will be assessed throughout the study by monitoring the following:

- Adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs).
- Clinical laboratory tests (haematology, biochemistry, liver function, renal function, urinalysis).
- Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, body temperature).
- 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG).
- Physical examination findings.
- Concomitant medication use.

**6.2 Safety Monitoring Plan**

An independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will be convened to review accumulating safety data. The DSMB will include members with expertise in hepatology, endocrinology, and clinical pharmacology. The DSMB will meet at the following time points:

- After the first 20 participants have completed 12 weeks of treatment.
- After all participants have completed 24 weeks of treatment.
- At any time if a safety concern is identified by the sponsor or the investigator.

The DSMB will provide written recommendations to the sponsor regarding the continuation, modification, or termination of the study. The sponsor will communicate these recommendations to the relevant ethics committees and health authorities as required.

**7. ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS**

**7.1 Independent Ethics Committee / Institutional Review Board**

The protocol, the informed consent form, and all participant-facing materials will be submitted to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of each participating site for review and written approval prior to study initiation. The study will not commence at any site until written IRB approval has been obtained. Any amendments to the protocol or informed consent form will be submitted for IRB review and approval before implementation, except where necessary to eliminate an immediate hazard to participants.

The IRB will be conducted in accordance with the Singapore Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (SGGCP) and applicable local regulations.

**7.2 Ethical Conduct of the Study**

The study will be conducted in accordance with the ethical principles that have their origin in the Declaration of Helsinki, the SGGCP, and the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) regulations. The investigator is responsible for ensuring that the study is conducted in full conformance with these principles and with the current protocol.

**7.3 Informed Consent**

Written informed consent will be obtained from each participant before any study-specific procedure is performed. The investigator or a designated qualified delegate will explain the nature, purpose, risks, and potential benefits of the study, as well as the participant's rights and responsibilities. Participants will be given ample time to consider their participation and will be encouraged to ask questions. A copy of the signed and dated informed consent form will be provided to the participant.

For participants who are unable to read, the informed consent form will be read to them in the presence of an impartial witness. Consent will be documented with the participant's thumbprint or mark, and the witness will sign and date the form.

**7.4 Participant Confidentiality**

All participant data will be handled in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA) of Singapore. Participant identifiers will be replaced by a unique participant number. The participant's identity will not be disclosed in any report or publication arising from this study. The investigator will maintain a confidential participant identification list linking participant numbers to personal identifiers, and this list will be stored securely in a locked facility with restricted access.

**7.5 Compensation for Injury**

Participants who sustain injury as a direct result of study participation will be entitled to medical treatment at no cost. Compensation for any permanent disability or death will be provided in accordance with the sponsor's insurance policy. Details of the insurance coverage will be provided to participants in the informed consent form.

**8. REGULATORY COMPLIANCE**

**8.1 Health Sciences Authority (HSA) Notification**

This study will be conducted under a Clinical Trial Certificate (CTC) obtained from HSA. The sponsor is responsible for submitting the clinical trial application to HSA and for obtaining approval prior to the commencement of the study. Any substantial amendments to the protocol will be submitted to HSA for approval prior to implementation.

**8.2 Protocol Amendments**

Any change to the protocol will be documented in a formal protocol amendment. Substantial amendments (e.g., changes to eligibility criteria, dosing regimen, or primary endpoint) will require prior IRB and HSA approval. Non-substantial administrative changes (e.g., correction of typographical errors) will be documented and submitted to the IRB for information.

**8.3 Protocol Deviations**

The investigator will not deviate from the protocol without prior written approval from the sponsor and the IRB, except where necessary to eliminate an immediate hazard to a participant. Any deviation, whether intentional or unintentional, will be documented and reported to the sponsor and the IRB in accordance with local requirements. The site will maintain a log of all protocol deviations.
